memory_candidates.content: In this repo's orchestrator scripts, skill_postflight_update (scripts/skill-base.sh) has its own internal status-vocabulary case switch, separate from update-task-status.sh's target_status validation. Adding a new postflight-reachable status value (e.g. "partial") to a caller's dispatch_status case arm is not sufficient by itself -- skill_postflight_update's own switch must also gain a matching case arm, or the call silently no-ops (falls into its '*) Non-success status ... skipped' default) even though update-task-status.sh itself already accepts and validates that target_status. Always grep skill_postflight_update's case statement directly before assuming a new status value will actually write.

orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's single-slot aux_pending[$t] write means multiple aux-signal-eligible conditions (drift-inspection, blocker-research, divergence-audit) can fire in the same postflight run for the same dispatch_status shape (e.g. partial+blockers[] below the drift threshold); whichever write runs last wins. When widening an aux-signal gate to cover a new case, check whether hard_mode already has an equivalent escalation mechanism for that same dispatch_status/handoff shape (it usually does, via the WORK (k) churn detector) and scope the new gate to hard_mode != true if so, to avoid the new gate silently starving the existing mechanism's aux signal on every hard-mode cycle.
